freeze_rule: AIFC v1.0 MUST NOT be labeled FROZEN unless every required check has machine-verifiable PASS evidence. Normative release gates and the admission-authority order must be resolved from immutable or lineage-bound identities rather than caller-supplied documents. Derived inherited obligations use their own immutable domain-separated hash profile. Assurance hash-profile semantics are versioned and content-bound. Gate replacement is forbidden until predecessor/successor gate definitions and all proof atoms are authoritatively anchored and the transition proof is authority-closed. Existing assurance, cryptographic, historical-key, freshness, causal, source-proof, statistics, cross-implementation, publication, and external-bench requirements remain mandatory.
forbidden_shortcuts: allowing a caller to supply the normative predecessor or successor release-gate document
deriving inherited obligations from an unregistered release-gate document
changing the admission-authority partial-order bytes while retaining the same order identifier
changing assurance-evidence-hash/v1 domain framing, canonicalization, implementation source or member schemas under the same profile identifier
hashing inherited gate obligations with an undocumented or non-domain-separated serialization
retroactively adding inherited-gate-obligation-set/v1 to assurance-evidence-hash/v1
accepting a predecessor gate definition merely because its gate_id matches the removed gate
accepting successor gate definitions merely because their human gate IDs match
treating symbolic Boolean atom names as executable semantic identity
allowing a transition proof to create or select the normative semantics that constitute its own theorem
allowing a normative root to self-authenticate through a descendant transition
treating equal scalar admission ranks as scientific or authority equivalence
promoting FORWARD_NULL_CONSISTENT_MISS to FORWARD_NULL_INCOMPATIBILITY_CANDIDATE under a same-rank shortcut
allowing a successor or harness to supply the set of inherited mandatory predecessor gates
omitting a predecessor mandatory gate from the inherited obligation set
accepting a gate-lineage transition because its hashes are structurally well-formed without resolving the referenced objects and executing the strengthening verifier
accepting FAKE_GATE_STRENGTHENING_RECEIPT evidence
changing validator implementation bytes or dependency semantics while retaining the same validator-semantics label
using only a human-readable validator semantics name as the acceptance-language identity
using Git blob SHA-1 as the sole protocol cryptographic identity for registered schema source bytes
silently bypassing a mandatory predecessor verifier layer
dropping an inherited mandatory FAIL gate from a successor result without a verified strengthening transition
removing a mandatory release gate because it remains BLOCKED
changing an issued schema identifier's acceptance language under the same schema ID
reusing an issued normative profile ID for an incompatible framing or semantic mapping

treating successful Ed25519 verification as proof that the key was historically uncompromised
treating registry-local ACTIVE status as proof that no later evidence retroactively invalidates the receipt
treating a cryptographically valid stale receipt as fresh evidence

parsing JSON Schema source with duplicate-key last-key-wins semantics
treating a content-hash-valid object as protocol-valid without Draft 2020-12 runtime schema admission

dropping attack vectors after observing failures
using one implementation twice as independent implementations

creating any trial before an externally certified frozen experiment plan exists

allowing post-CREATED operator generator choice for strongest-grade v1
reconstructing or sanitizing the conditioning view after target observation
trusting a producer-selected future event without deterministic selector replay

selecting an entropy/security justification after observing the target
accepting dangling evidence hashes without exact-byte resolution
counting multiple witness IDs in one failure domain as independent quorum members
using a disconnected or unauthorized witness-registry transition
accepting noncanonical rational bounds
using the fixed-horizon product formula outside its frozen theorem conditions
placing a release manifest inside the source commit whose SHA it claims to bind
